findings.evidence: Statement at line 71-77 binds `{K L : Type*}`; `L` appears only in the RHS `ClassGroup.mk L ...`. All three in-file uses must write it by hand: `mulEquiv_mk (K := FractionRing R) (L := FractionRing T)` (mulEquiv_trans), and likewise in `mulEquiv_refl`. Mathlib's analogues `ClassGroup.equiv_mk (K' : Type*)` (Basic.lean:207) and `FractionalIdeal.ringEquivOfRingEquiv_trans_apply (M : Type*)` (Operations.lean:993) take the target explicitly.
findings.fix: Make `L` explicit — `theorem mulEquiv_mk (L : Type*) [Field L] [Algebra S L] [IsFractionRing S L] ...` — matching `ClassGroup.equiv_mk (K' : Type*)` and `ClassGroup.mk_canonicalEquiv (K' : Type*)`.
findings.issue: In `mulEquiv_mk`, `L` (and its `Field`/`Algebra`/`IsFractionRing` instances) is implicit but occurs only on the right-hand side, so `rw [mulEquiv_mk]` leaves it as a metavariable; the target fraction field is never inferable.

findings.evidence: Line 46 `private theorem mulEquiv_mk_fractionRing`; Mathlib `noncomputable def ClassGroup.mulEquiv` carries `@[simps!]` (Basic.lean:459-460), whose generated `ClassGroup.mulEquiv_apply` is a simp lemma and is used at line 56 of this file.
findings.fix: Make the `FractionRing`-specialized computation public and `@[simp]` (LHS `mulEquiv f (mk (FractionRing R) I)` is fully determined), keeping the general `mulEquiv_mk` as the `rw`-form.
findings.issue: No public lemma lets `simp` compute `ClassGroup.mulEquiv f (ClassGroup.mk _ I)`: `mulEquiv_mk` cannot be `@[simp]` (see above) and the only fully-determined form, `mulEquiv_mk_fractionRing`, is `private`. A consumer running `simp` on such a term instead hits Mathlib's `@[simps!]`-generated `ClassGroup.mulEquiv_apply`, which unfolds into the `ClassGroup.equiv`/`QuotientGroup.congr` composite — exactly the unfolding this file exists to prevent.

findings.evidence: `ClassGroup.mk0` (Basic.lean:253) and `ClassGroup.mk_mk0` (Basic.lean:257) are the standard entry points for classes of integral ideals; grep of Mathlib's FractionalIdeal files shows only `ringEquivOfRingEquiv_{apply,apply_val,trans,trans_apply,refl,spanSingleton}` (Operations.lean:971-1005) — no `coeIdeal` interaction.
findings.fix: Add `mulEquiv_mk0 [IsDedekindDomain R] [IsDedekindDomain S] (f : R ≃+* S) (I : (Ideal R)⁰) : mulEquiv f (ClassGroup.mk0 I) = ClassGroup.mk0 ⟨Ideal.map f I, _⟩`, via `ClassGroup.mk_mk0` plus a `ringEquivOfRingEquiv_coeIdeal` step.
findings.issue: The stated consumer — the genus-field argument that `I · σI` is principal — works with nonzero integral ideals, i.e. `ClassGroup.mk0`, but the file provides no computation of `mulEquiv f (ClassGroup.mk0 I)`, and there is no lemma relating `FractionalIdeal.ringEquivOfRingEquiv f` to `Ideal.map f` on coerced integral ideals, so the bridge must be rebuilt downstream.

summary: The functorial laws and their pointwise forms are complete and correctly annotated, but the headline characteristic lemma `mulEquiv_mk` has an undeterminable implicit type argument and no simp-usable specialization, so consumers cannot actually compute with the new API without named arguments or falling back to Mathlib's raw `mulEquiv_apply` unfolding.
